title: India beat England in thrilling Mumbai run fest to reach T20 World Cup final
content:
India survived a blistering century from Jacob Bethell to defeat England by seven runs and secure their passage into Sunday’s T20 World Cup final against New Zealand.

The holders batted brilliantly in front of a capacity, partisan crowd at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai to rattle up the fourth-highest total ever scored by a team at this tournament.

Man-of-the-match Sanju Samson contributed a scintillating 89 off 42 balls, with England left to rue their captain, Harry Brook, putting down a simple chance offered by the India opener when he had only 15.

That drop contrasted markedly with India’s fielding with Axar Patel, running at speed towards the boundary and taking the ball at full stretch as he dived forward, to dismiss Brook for only seven from Jasprit Bumrah’s first delivery of the night. He produced an equally outstanding grab late on that helped see off the dangerous Will Jacks.

Yet Bethell, who smashed 105 off 48 deliveries — with eight fours and seven sixes along the way — found sufficient support, particularly from Jacks (35 off 20 balls), to push the co-hosts close.

Excellent overs from Bumrah and Hardik Pandya in the 18th and 19th effectively snuffed out England’s challenge. Bumrah conceded just 33 from his allocation, going at 8.25 per over in a match where the overall scoring rate was 12.5.

“He is a world-class and once-in-a-generation bowler, and that is what he showed today,” said Samson of Bumrah. “This player of the match award should go to him, actually, because if he didn’t bowl that well in the last 10 overs, I wouldn’t be standing here.”

Jofra Archer still hit Shivam Dube’s last three legitimate balls of the match for six, but by then it was in a losing cause.

In all, there were a staggering 499 runs across the game’s 40 overs, the highest ever aggregate score at the tournament — beating the previous record by 40 runs. The 34 sixes struck were also the most in a T20 World Cup fixture.

India’s daunting total had been built around another glorious innings from Samson, who followed his 97 not out against West Indies by running riot in Mumbai in the wake of Brook’s costly drop.

He struck eight fours and seven sixes to set a breathless tone.

“I gave myself a bit of extra time — I calculated my innings and that’s why things came off really nicely,” Samson told the post-match presentation. “I know I was a bit lucky to start off with, but I just wanted to keep going because no score is stoppable here. Even 250 looks like it could be chased here.”

All of England’s bowlers suffered as Ishan Kishan (39 off 18 balls), Dube (43 off 25), Pandya (27 off 12) and Tilak Varma (21 off seven) made hay. The holders’ total included 19 sixes — the joint most in an innings at the tournament. Seven were struck off Archer, who returned figures of 1-61 from his four overs.

The 2024 winners will now travel to Ahmedabad for Sunday’s final hoping to retain their trophy. New Zealand are yet to win an ICC World Cup in any format.

That they remain the sport’s dominant force in the shortest format of the game.

Yes, they were thumped by South Africa earlier in the tournament and needed a stress-inducing win over West Indies in the Super Eights to reach this point. England gave them a real scare, too, and old questions about their reliance on Jasprit Bumrah — whose six-run 18th over was crucial to India sealing the deal — will resurface.

But in T20 internationals, where an over or an individual innings can make the difference, India’s strength in depth and star power across the XI makes them superior to everybody else, including their vanquished foes England.

Abhishek Sharma had appeared to be the batter to be wary of entering this tournament, but he has struggled for fluency outside of a half-century against Zimbabwe. So up stepped Samson in their two most crucial games, racking up 186 runs at a strike rate of 202.2.

Mystery spinner Varun Chakravarthy picked up nine wickets in the group phase but has been expensive since, going for 64 from his quota against England. Yet his team-mates across all three departments picked up the slack admirably.

Timely contributions from Pandya, Dube and Ishan Kishan have repeatedly offset the struggles of captain Suryakumar Yadav and Verma.

Axar Patel, who has been in and out of the team, proved a point of difference against England with his efforts in the field, including a stunning catch to dismiss Brook, and a brilliant grab and flick back as he staggered over the boundary rope for team-mate Dube to collect and see off the dangerous Will Jacks.

Now, having prevailed in Mumbai, they must exorcise any ghosts fans believe haunted the team at Ahmedabad’s Narendra Modi Stadium, where they lost the 2023 ODI World Cup final to Australia.

New Zealand will be awkward opponents. They have shown resilience and risen to the occasion brilliantly across a memorable run to the final. But once again, the depth and star power India possess could prove the difference — as it has time and again for them in this tournament.

Anantaajith Raghuraman
